To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the three green opsin genes of medaka fish (Oryzais latipes) are orthologous genes derived from a triplication in a common ancestor of the genus, (2) the spectral properties of the three genes have been diverged in the course of evolution, and (3) the spectral divergence of the two paralogous genes has proceeded through gene conversion and amino acid replacement, and the spectral difference is attributed to a few amino acid replacements.

the spectral differences of the three green opsin genes among the Oryzias fish are largely explained by the amino acid differences between the two paralogous opsins and that the divergence of the orthologous green opsin gene in the latipes species was accelerated by a few amino acid replacements.
The spectral divergence of orthologue RH2 A opsin genes was observed among the three species groups of Oryzias, whereas the paralogues, RH2 B and 2C, were spectrally conserved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the green opsin gene has evolved in the medaka fish.
the evolution of green opsins in teleost fish and their role in color vision.
the molecular evolution of the green opsin genes, and the results provide new insights into the evolution of phototransduction in medaka fish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spectral divergence of green opsin genes is not necessarily conserved or conserved in a species specific manner.

the spectral divergence of green opsins is a common feature in the genus Oryzias, and that the divergence is largely driven by the orthologous divergence in the latipes group, whereas the paralogous divergence of RH2 B/C is suppressed by gene conversion.
the spectral differentiation of the three RH2 genes in medaka is a result of the combination of orthologous divergence and paralogous anticonvergence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RH2 A, B, and C genes in the medaka fish were derived from a triplication event and that their spectral differentiation was largely driven by positive selection.
gene duplications of green opsins in medaka fish are accompanied by paralogous anticonvergence and orthologous divergence.

the three green opsin genes have been maintained in the Oryzias lineage for at least 20 30 million years, and that the spectral divergence of orthology and paralogy of green opsin genes has been driven by the different ecological and/or behavioral requirements of the species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three green opsins in medaka are not orthologous, but rather paralogous.
spectral divergence of the green opsin genes was driven by different forces in orthologous and in paralogous genes.
spectral differentiation of green opsin genes is a common phenomenon in medaka fish.
